Rolex · ref. 16700

GMT-Master

Pilot's · 38–40mm · 50–100m · automatic
Photo: gabihil · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

The Rolex GMT-Master is a pilot's watch designed to show the time in two different time zones simultaneously. Its signature design cue is a two-tone, 24-hour rotating bezel, often in blue and red, earning it the nickname "Pepsi".

The story

Developed in the 1950s in collaboration with Pan American World Airways, the GMT-Master was created for their pilots on long-haul flights. The first model, reference 6542, was introduced in 1954 and featured a Bakelite bezel insert that was later replaced with aluminum due to its fragility. The next generation, reference 1675, introduced in 1959, increased the case size to 40mm and added crown guards for better protection. A significant technical update came with the reference 16750 in the early 1980s, which housed a new caliber with a quickset date function. The final series, reference 16700, was produced from 1988 to 1999, co-existing for a time with the newer GMT-Master II line before being discontinued.
